TrustDemo

The official URL for this implementation guide is: 

http://smart.who.int/trust-demo/ImplementationGuide/smart.who.int.trust-demo

The user journeys of one cross-border family, told as journeys (birth-dose DVCs in Taifafeki, CHW registration and triage read in Onesa, clinic verification, vaccine-code mapping and schedule, family VHLs on one phone, viewed and audited back in Taifafeki) as a WHO SMART Guidelines L2 DAK and L3 implementation guide, built on the SMART Trust HCERT libraries.

resource.name: Birth clinic issuing system
resource.description:
The hospital system abroad that issues a DVC per dose with the HCERT library: the HCERT issuing system (smart-trust-tools) of a trust network participant (XXR).

**Persona**: Software that calls the library once per dose and never holds the private key; signs only with a DSC its country's CSCA issued and has already shared with the GDHCN.

**Also known as**: Issuer of the birth-dose DVCs (SMART Trust Issuer)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- Kesaro Provincial Hospital system, Taifafeki (Country A, XXR)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J1 — Born abroad](scenarios.html#j1--born-abroad-taifafeki-birth-day): J1 An Onesan baby is born in Taifafeki

**On the device screens**: [S1 Birth Abroad & Printed DVC QR Cards (Dr. Anan's tablet)](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/demo/S1/)

**Discussed in the workshop modules**: [M1 From journey to capabilities](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m1/); [M4 Trust, credentials and wallets](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m4/); [M5 Governance, decision rights and the legal basis](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m5/)

resource.description:

**Persona**: A parent carrying a newborn's records across borders on paper and one shared phone; no health training, little time, limited connectivity.

**Also known as**: VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL); Holder (SMART Trust)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- ![Bounmy](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Bounmy](personas.html#bounmy-father--holds-the-family-phone-onesa), Bounmy SENGMANY (father, holds the family phone)
- ![Khamla](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Khamla](personas.html#khamla-mother-onesa), Khamla SENGMANY (mother)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J1 — Born abroad](scenarios.html#j1--born-abroad-taifafeki-birth-day): J1 An Onesan baby is born in Taifafeki
- [J2 — Found at home](scenarios.html#j2--found-at-home-onesa-3-weeks-later): J2a A health worker finds the baby — and reads his cards; J2b Registered at home, and referred
- [J3 — Made official](scenarios.html#j3--made-official-lomaru-district-health-center-4-weeks-later): J3a The clinic confirms the cards are genuine; J3b Taifafeki vaccines are fitted to the Onesan schedule
- [J4.0 — Crossing back: one family, one phone](scenarios.html#j40--crossing-back-one-family-one-phone-onesa-12-months-later): J4.0a One phone holds the whole family’s records (told through Bounmy); J4.0b Dad creates a link to share at the clinic (told through Bounmy)

**Discussed in the workshop modules**: [M1 From journey to capabilities](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m1/); [M2 The reference architecture and where you stand](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m2/); [M3 Standards, specifications and the core data set](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m3/); [M4 Trust, credentials and wallets](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m4/); [M5 Governance, decision rights and the legal basis](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m5/); [M6 Doing it once, together](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m6/); [M7 Our first move, what it costs, and what we ask for](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m7/)

**User stories** ([all stories](scenarios.html#user-stories)):

- I want to have my son's birth doses from abroad recognised at home, so that his care does not start over and nothing is repeated
- I want to show each family member's records abroad from our one shared phone, with a passcode I can say aloud, so that a doctor abroad can treat us without paper or an app
- I want to decide who sees my child's record, and for how long, so that the record stays at home and I know who has looked

- [J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs](business-processes.html#j40-issue-the-familys-records-to-one-phone-as-vhls): Choose who to share, with a passcode and an expiry

resource.name: CHW app
resource.description:
The OHS app on the CHW's phone: reads a foreign DVC without verifying it (triage read, STT-VER-011), registers the child and records a referral, all offline, syncing later.

**Persona**: Offline-first Android app; must never present an unverified record as verified.

**Also known as**: Triage reader (SMART Trust Receiver, read-unverified)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- CHW app, Onesa (Country B)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J2 — Found at home](scenarios.html#j2--found-at-home-onesa-3-weeks-later): J2a A health worker finds the baby — and reads his cards; J2b Registered at home, and referred

**On the device screens**: [S2 Offline QR Scan of the Foreign Cards (Vilay's phone)](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/demo/S2/); [S3 Newborn Registration & Clinic Referral (Vilay's phone)](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/demo/S3/)

**Discussed in the workshop modules**: [M2 The reference architecture and where you stand](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m2/); [M3 Standards, specifications and the core data set](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m3/); [M4 Trust, credentials and wallets](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m4/); [M5 Governance, decision rights and the legal basis](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m5/)

**Lanes and tasks in the business processes**:

- [J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B](business-processes.html#j2-discover-and-refer-an-unregistered-infant-in-country-b): Read each DVC unverified (triage); Add the infant; save doses as reported; Create a referral to the home clinic for verification

resource.description:
Finds unregistered children on home visits, registers them and refers them to the clinic (J2).

**Persona**: Works on foot and offline, on a cheap Android phone; registers and refers, never judges authenticity.

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- ![Vilay](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Vilay](personas.html#vilay-community-health-worker--village-04-onesa), Vilay (community health worker, Village 04, Onesa)

**On the device screens**: [S2 Offline QR Scan of the Foreign Cards (Vilay's phone)](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/demo/S2/); [S3 Newborn Registration & Clinic Referral (Vilay's phone)](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/demo/S3/)

**Discussed in the workshop modules**: [M2 The reference architecture and where you stand](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m2/); [M3 Standards, specifications and the core data set](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m3/); [M4 Trust, credentials and wallets](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m4/); [M5 Governance, decision rights and the legal basis](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m5/)

**User stories** ([all stories](scenarios.html#user-stories)):

- I want to read a foreign vaccination QR offline and register the child with it, so that the clinic sees what was given before the family arrives
- I want to refer a child whose foreign record needs checking, so that verification is done by someone who can
- I want to register a newborn into the household offline, before civil registration, so that no newborn in my village is missed, even with no signal

resource.name: GDHCN trust anchor
resource.description:
WHO's GDHCN, which receives participants' PKI material and distributes it as DID trust lists; Trust Network Anchor (SMART Trust), Trust Anchor (IHE ITI VHL).

**Persona**: A WHO service publishing DID documents over did:web; verifiers fetch it when online and keep a copy.

**Also known as**: Trust Network Anchor (SMART Trust); Trust Anchor (IHE ITI VHL)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- GDHCN DEV trust network (WHO)

resource.name: Home clinic EHR
resource.description:
The clinic's OHS-based record system: verifies DVCs against the GDHCN trust list, imports them as FHIR Immunization resources and evaluates the national schedule (J3).

**Persona**: Holds the DID trust list from its last refresh, about weekly for a clinic without its own connection, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office; loading it is a precondition of a visit, and it verifies offline at the point of care.

**Also known as**: Verifier at the home clinic (SMART Trust Receiver)

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- Lomaru District Health Center EHR (Country B)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J3 — Made official](scenarios.html#j3--made-official-lomaru-district-health-center-4-weeks-later): J3a The clinic confirms the cards are genuine; J3b Taifafeki vaccines are fitted to the Onesan schedule

resource.name: Home clinic provider
resource.description:
The nurse at the home clinic who receives the referral, has the foreign DVCs verified and decides catch-up doses (J3).

**Persona**: Trusts the system's verdict and needs a reason when a certificate fails.

**Played in the journeys by** (fictional):

- ![Chanthason](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) [Chanthason](personas.html#chanthason-nurse--district-health-center-onesa), Nurse Chanthason (Lomaru District Health Center, Onesa)

**In the user scenarios**:

- [J3 — Made official](scenarios.html#j3--made-official-lomaru-district-health-center-4-weeks-later): J3a The clinic confirms the cards are genuine (told through Chanthason); J3b Taifafeki vaccines are fitted to the Onesan schedule (told through Chanthason)

**On the device screens**: [S4 Clinic Referral & GDHCN Verification (Chanthason's tablet)](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/demo/S4/); [S5 Terminology Adjudication & National Schedule (Chanthason's tablet)](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/demo/S5/)

**Discussed in the workshop modules**: [M1 From journey to capabilities](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m1/); [M3 Standards, specifications and the core data set](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m3/); [M4 Trust, credentials and wallets](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m4/); [M6 Doing it once, together](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/m6/)

**User stories** ([all stories](scenarios.html#user-stories)):

- I want to know whether a foreign certificate is genuine, and why not when it is not
- I want to see which doses are due once the foreign doses are imported, so that I give only what is missing

resource.description:
How it is used: J2 onwards. Vilay registers Somsak on a home visit, and the same patient carries every Onesan record that follows: the verified Taifafeki doses, the Onesan doses and the summary shared in J4.

Why: a child born abroad is not in the Onesan civil registry yet. resource.description:
How it is used: J2b. The CHW refers Somsak to the district health center to have his foreign cards verified and his doses fitted to the Onesan schedule.

resource.name: Onesa: dose on the national schedule
resource.description:
How it is used: J3 and after. These are the Taifafeki birth doses once the district clinic has verified them, and every dose given in Onesa.

Why: the Onesan schedule engine works on Onesan EPI codes, so each dose must carry one. A dose that came from abroad keeps the issuer's product code beside the Onesan one, added through the ConceptMap and confirmed by the nurse. Nothing the other country said is overwritten. A verified foreign dose is recorded from its primary source, the signing hospital, and its Provenance says how it was verified.

resource.name: Onesa: every VHL access logged at home
resource.description:
How it is used: J4.1. The Onesan national gateway records each attempt by a clinic abroad to fetch a family member's VHL manifest, the refused ones included.

Why: the family shares a link, not a copy, and the data stays in Onesa. Logging every access at home, following IHE Basic Audit Log Patterns, is what lets the family and the ministry see who looked, from where and when. A wrong passcode is logged too.

resource.name: Onesa: foreign dose as reported (not yet verified)
resource.description:
How it is used: J2b. The CHW app reads each Taifafeki paper DVC offline without checking its signature, and saves the dose like this.

Why: a CHW phone may have no trust list and no signal, but the doses should not be lost. Recording them with primarySource false, the paper card as the report origin and the family named in the note keeps them visibly "reported, not verified". The schedule will not count them until a clinic verifies them (J3). Only the issuer's product code is present, because mapping to the Onesan schedule is a clinical step for later.

resource.name: Onesa: foreign DVC verified against the GDHCN trust list
resource.description:
How it is used: J3a. The district EHR verifies each Taifafeki DVC offline against its cached copy of the GDHCN trust list, then imports the dose. This record says so.

Why: a verified dose replaces a reported one, so the record must show who verified what, against which policy, and which reported doses it removes. Anyone who later doubts a dose can follow this record back to the signed certificate and the issuing country's key.

resource.name: Onesa: household on the CHW's roster
resource.description:
How it is used: J2a. The CHW finds that a newborn is missing from the household roster and adds Somsak as a member.

Why: Onesan community health work is organized by household. The roster is how a CHW notices that a child is missing, and it is the unit the family phone shares under in J4 (one phone, three profiles).

resource.name: Onesa: newborn registration captured offline
resource.description:
How it is used: J2a. These are the CHW's answers on the newborn registration form, which the app renders with Structured Data Capture and saves with no signal.

Why: in Onesa the form is the configuration, not code. A ministry can change the questions without shipping a new app. The answers are kept so that the Patient and Group extracted from them can always be traced back to what was asked and who answered.

resource.name: Taifafeki: dose given at the birth hospital (DVC source)
resource.description:
How it is used: J1. Each birth dose (Hep B, BCG) that Dr Anan gives is recorded here first. The hospital then packs it into a Digital Vaccination Certificate (HCERT, signed with XXR's key) and prints it as a QR card.

Why: the DVC can only carry what this record holds. The vaccine product, date, lot, dose number and the administering organization are exactly the fields the HCERT certificate needs. They are required here so every printed card is complete. The product is coded from the WHO PreQual-style product list, because that is the code Onesa will later map to its own schedule (J3).

resource.name: Taifafeki: Hep B birth dose, as the hospital records and signs it
resource.description: The record behind the first DVC Khamla carries home: product, date, lot, dose number and performer, the fields the HCERT certificate carries.

resource.name: Taifafeki: newborn at the birth hospital
resource.description:
How it is used: J1. Kesaro Provincial Hospital registers Somsak under its own hospital number on the day he is born.

Why: a baby born to Onesan parents in Taifafeki has no Taifafeki citizen id, so the hospital number is the only identifier the hospital can put behind the dose records it signs. The DVCs it prints carry the name and date of birth, not this number. The family's home country therefore cannot rely on any Taifafeki identifier, and links the doses to its own patient (see the Onesan patient profile).

resource.name: Taifafeki: record of a summary read through a VHL
resource.description:
How it is used: J4.1. The Kesaro clinic viewer keeps this record when it opens Somsak's patient summary through the Verifiable Health Link that his father shows.

Why: the Taifafeki clinic views the Onesan record and does not copy it into a Taifafeki registry. So the clinic keeps a note of what it saw, where it came from, and how it was verified: the VHL's signature against Onesa's key on the GDHCN trust list, the manifest fetch, and the passcode. The Onesan side keeps its own log of the same access (the Onesan audit profile).
